hero.subtitle: A place of practice and spiritual cultivation founded by Venerable Thích Phổ Ứng in 1953, located in District 4, Ho Chi Minh City.

about.title: Over 70 Years
about.founding: Tịnh xá Linh Quang was founded in 1953 by Venerable Thích Phổ Ứng (Thích Nhuận Tắc), a disciple of the Great Master Huệ Nhựt (1903–1983), as a simple retreat for meditation and spiritual practice.
about.rebuild: In 1963, the temple was rebuilt on a 1,250m² site. In 1992, it underwent a major renovation, becoming a stable place of practice for monastics and lay Buddhists alike.
about.architecture: The main hall reflects the "Three Grades of Rebirth" architectural motif: the upper section carved with lotus pond reliefs, the middle adorned with embossed lotus pond patterns, and the lower a "blue water pond" bordered in earthen brick — symbolizing the path toward liberation.

activities.title: Practice And
activities.subtitle: The temple is not only a place of practice but also a source of compassion through decades of charitable work.
activities.item1Desc: Established in 1989, an education center helping children with disabilities integrate into the community.
activities.item2Desc: Operating since 1995, offering free consultations and medication to those in need.
activities.item3Desc: Held annually on the 16th day of the first lunar month, honoring the founding Venerable's legacy.
activities.item4Desc: Meditation, sutra chanting, and dharma talks for monastics and lay Buddhists alike.

historyPage.title: The Journey Of
historyPage.subtitle: From a simple meditation retreat to a place of practice and compassionate service — the history of Tịnh xá Linh Quang across more than seven decades.
historyPage.earlyDaysDesc1: In 1952, guided by the vow to spread the Dharma of the Mendicant Mahayana order founded by the great teacher Huệ Nhựt, the Venerable Elder Phổ Ứng arrived in the Vĩnh Hội area of District 4.
historyPage.earlyDaysDesc2: At that time, District 4 was still a riverside district home to many poor laborers. Material life was scarce and living conditions difficult, while the community's need for a place of spiritual refuge kept growing.
historyPage.earlyDaysDesc3: Finding a plot of land to build a temple amid such a densely populated area was extremely difficult. Yet through the monk's steadfast resolve and the support of devoted lay Buddhists, the Venerable remained determined to stay and plant the seeds of the Dharma there.
historyPage.earlyDaysDesc4: By 1953, a small thatched hermitage had been built on what is now Nguyễn Khoái Street.
historyPage.earlyDaysDesc5: Though humble, with a thatched roof and wooden walls, it became a gathering place for followers of the Buddha — where the first sounds of the bell, the wooden fish, and sutra chanting rang out over the Vĩnh Hội area.
historyPage.earlyDaysDesc6: From that small hermitage, the seed of Tịnh xá Linh Quang began to grow.
historyPage.constructionDesc1: After nearly a decade of steady practice and guiding lay Buddhists, more and more people came to the temple. The original thatched hermitage could no longer meet the needs of the monastic community and its followers.
historyPage.constructionDesc2: In 1963, Venerable Phổ Ứng, together with the monastic community and many lay Buddhists, began a major reconstruction. Amid a country still in turmoil, building a proper monastery was no easy task. Every brick and every column was raised through the combined effort of monks and lay Buddhists alike — some contributed labor, some contributed funds, some could only give a day's work at a time, but all shared the same aspiration to build the Triple Gem's home.
historyPage.constructionDesc3: After three years of construction, in 1966, Tịnh xá Linh Quang was officially completed. The central sanctuary was built in a solemn, harmonious style, rich in Vietnamese Buddhist architecture. Remarkably, this same sanctuary remains almost entirely intact today, standing as a historical witness to more than half a century of growth.
historyPage.constructionDesc4: From then on, Tịnh xá Linh Quang became not only a place of worship but also a center of monastic study — sustaining regular sutra chanting, dharma teaching, and the spiritual life of many generations of Buddhists.
historyPage.founderEraDesc1: Over thirty years as abbot, Venerable Phổ Ứng devoted himself wholeheartedly to laying the foundation for the temple. He held monastic discipline as the bedrock, and placed training capable monastics and guiding lay Buddhists at the center of his work. Under his guidance, Tịnh xá Linh Quang gradually became one of the leading centers of the Mendicant Mahayana order in southern Vietnam.
historyPage.founderEraDesc2: Beyond caring for the monastic community's practice, the Venerable always kept the temple's doors open to those seeking to worship, hear the Dharma, and find peace in their lives. In 1983, having fulfilled his vow to spread the Dharma, the Venerable passed away peacefully, closing thirty years of founding and building the order.
historyPage.successionTitle: Continuing The Lineage Under Venerable Từ Giang
historyPage.successionDesc1: After Venerable Phổ Ứng's passing, Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang inherited the lineage and became the second abbot of Tịnh xá Linh Quang.
historyPage.successionDesc2: Carrying forward his teacher's aspirations, Hòa Thượng not only sustained the temple's practice but also expanded its Buddhist activities, gradually turning Tịnh xá Linh Quang into a leading center of Buddhist life in District 4.
historyPage.successionDesc3: With a long-term vision, he recognized the need for more space to serve the monastic community. In 1994, construction began on a lecture hall and monks' quarters, completed in 1995. The structure to the right of the sanctuary (facing the temple courtyard) became a place for:
historyPage.successionBullet3: The kitchen and dining hall serving the community.
historyPage.successionDesc4: This construction marked an important milestone for Tịnh xá Linh Quang, creating favorable conditions for practice and the spread of the Dharma in the decades that followed.
historyPage.successionDesc5: Alongside developing the physical grounds, Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang placed special emphasis on engaging with the wider community. Under his guidance, the temple maintained regular sutra chanting, held major ceremonies such as Vesak and Vu Lan, prayers for peace and for the deceased, and expanded free medical care, social charity, and support for the poor. These efforts helped make Tịnh xá Linh Quang a familiar address for the people of District 4 and surrounding areas.
historyPage.thirdAbbotDesc1: In 2021, after Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang's passing, the Vietnam Buddhist Sangha appointed Thượng Tọa Thích Minh Huệ as the third abbot of Tịnh xá Linh Quang.
historyPage.thirdAbbotDesc2: Continuing the teachings of his predecessors, the Venerable and the monastic community have kept the monastery's traditions, sustaining regular practice sessions, traditional ceremonies, and the charitable work that has long been part of Tịnh xá Linh Quang's character.
historyPage.thirdAbbotDesc3: Alongside caring for monastic practice, this period has seen the temple transform how it preserves and shares its history. Many documents, photographs, and memories of the temple's founding and growth have been gathered and organized; its activities are now shared more widely through digital platforms, helping connect Buddhists near and far and preserving this heritage for future generations.
historyPage.thirdAbbotDesc4: As of 2026, more than 73 years after the first thatched hermitage was built, Tịnh xá Linh Quang remains a place of quiet practice in the heart of the city. From a simple thatched hut, it has grown into an ancestral temple with a venerable sanctuary, a lecture hall, monks' quarters, and many other facilities — and remains a spiritual anchor for generations of monastics, Buddhists, and residents alike.
historyPage.lineageIntro: More than seven decades of history at Tịnh xá Linh Quang have been shaped by the dedication of three generations of abbots:
historyPage.lineageFounderLine: The founder, who planted the first seeds of the temple.
historyPage.lineagePastAbbotLine: The successor, who expanded the temple into a center of practice, teaching, and service to society.
historyPage.lineageAbbotLine: The current abbot, continuing the tradition, preserving the founders' legacy, and carrying its values into a new era.
historyPage.lineageClosing: Three generations, one lineage, united by a single aspiration: to serve the Dharma, to benefit all beings, and to keep the light of the Buddha's teaching shining at the heart of the city.

visitPage.title: Visit
visitPage.subtitle: Everything you need to know before visiting Tịnh xá Linh Quang — directions, opening hours, what to expect, and visiting etiquette.
visitPage.carDesc: From District 1 (near Independence Palace), follow Nam Kỳ Khởi Nghĩa – Nguyễn Thái Bình – Calmette Bridge – Bến Vân Đồn – Nguyễn Khoái, about 4km (15–20 minutes). The temple has space for parking.
visitPage.transitDesc: Take bus route 46, 38, 44, or 31, then walk about 20–30 minutes to reach the temple entrance.
visitPage.rideshareDesc: Ride-hailing services (including Green SM electric taxis) can take you directly to the temple gate on Nguyễn Khoái.
visitPage.activitiesSubtitle: Beyond a simple visit, Tịnh xá Linh Quang offers a full sensory experience of Buddhist life — from quiet architecture to shared ceremony. Here is what most visitors come to see and do.
visitPage.sightseeingDesc: Take a quiet walk through the grounds and admire the temple's "Three Grades of Rebirth" architecture — lotus pond reliefs above, embossed lotus motifs at the middle tier, and an earthen-bordered "blue water pond" below. Most visitors linger near the gate and courtyard, where the original 1963 stonework is still on display.
visitPage.prayDesc: Step into the main sanctuary and join monastics and lay Buddhists in quiet prayer before the central Buddha statue. The hall is open daily, so you can sit for a few quiet minutes of contemplation even outside of scheduled ceremonies.
visitPage.wishDesc: Light incense, offer flowers, and make a wish as part of the "cầu tự" tradition observed by many visitors before the altar. It's a quiet, personal ritual — take your time, and follow the lead of those already praying nearby.
visitPage.festivalDesc: Visit during major Buddhist festivals — including the founder's memorial ceremony each lunar new year — to see the temple decorated with lanterns and banners and observe ceremonies shared by the wider community. These are the liveliest, most colorful times to experience Linh Quang.
visitPage.scheduleSubtitle: The temple's day follows a fixed rhythm of practice, from the pre-dawn wake-up bell to the evening repentance ceremony.
visitPage.wakeDesc: The sound of the wooden board and bell signals the start of a new day — the community rises, dresses, and prepares for morning practice.
visitPage.morningPracticeDesc: The community gathers in the main sanctuary to chant sutras, recite mantras, and sit in meditation, opening the day with a calm and mindful heart.
visitPage.breakfastDesc: After morning practice, the monastics take breakfast in solemn mindfulness, nourishing the body to continue the day's Buddhist activities.
visitPage.choresDesc: Time for labor — tending the grounds, cleaning the temple, and other shared tasks. The spirit of "a day without work is a day without food" is practiced through every simple task.
visitPage.lotusSutraDesc: The community recites the Lotus Sutra together, one of the most important sutras of Mahayana Buddhism, to nurture wisdom and compassion.
visitPage.noonOfferingDesc: The offering to the Triple Gem and the midday meal are held in quiet solemnity, expressing gratitude and the practitioner's spirit of moderation.
visitPage.chantingDesc: Reciting the name of the Buddha helps settle the mind, nurture faith, and increase merit.
visitPage.restDesc: The community rests to recover their strength, preparing for the afternoon's practice sessions.
visitPage.studyDesc: The monastics spend time studying sutras, precepts, and treatises, deepening their understanding as a foundation for spreading the Dharma.
visitPage.eveningPracticeDesc: The evening chanting and practice session closes a day of labor in wakefulness and serenity.
visitPage.repentanceDesc: In the evening, the community performs the repentance ceremony together, reflecting on past faults, nurturing a compassionate heart, and vowing to progress on the path of practice.
visitPage.recurringSubtitle: Beyond the daily schedule, Tổ đình Linh Quang Tịnh Xá also holds regular activities for lay Buddhists.
visitPage.refugeDesc: Held for those who wish to formally become a Buddhist by taking refuge in the Triple Gem.
visitPage.repentanceChantingDesc: A shared practice session for both monastics and lay Buddhists.
visitPage.clinicDesc: Free charitable consultations and traditional medicine dispensed to those in need.
visitPage.dress: Wear modest, respectful clothing — avoid short or gaudy outfits.
visitPage.quiet: Speak and move gently to preserve the temple's quiet, reverent atmosphere.
visitPage.ceremony: Show respect and follow along quietly during any ongoing ceremony.
visitPage.noTouch: Do not touch statues or religious objects on display.
visitPage.noLitter: Do not litter within the temple grounds.
visitPage.noFood: Do not bring food into the worship areas.

mastersSection.subtitle: Thượng Tọa Thích Minh Huệ is the current abbot, carrying forward the practice and service of Tịnh xá Linh Quang across more than seven decades.
mastersSection.founderBio: Venerable Thích Phổ Ứng founded Tịnh xá Linh Quang in 1953 as a disciple of the Great Master Huệ Nhựt. He guided the temple through its founding and its 1963 rebuilding, laying the spiritual foundation that later abbots would carry forward.
mastersSection.pastAbbotBio: Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang served as abbot of Tịnh xá Linh Quang from 1983 until his passing in 2021. He led the temple's 1992 major renovation and founded its free clinic and education center for children with disabilities.
mastersSection.abbotBio: Thượng Tọa Thích Minh Huệ was appointed abbot of Tịnh xá Linh Quang in 2021, succeeding the late Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang. He continues the temple's charitable clinic, education center, and daily practice traditions.

masterDetail.journeyEyebrow: The Path To Becoming A Master

founder.intro: Venerable Thích Phổ Ứng (Dharma name Thích Nhuận Tắc) was a disciple of the Great Master Huệ Nhựt (1903–1983), one of the senior teachers of the Mendicant (Khất Sĩ) tradition. From a young age he devoted himself to monastic life, and after years of study and wandering practice under his teacher's guidance, he chose District 4, Saigon, as the place to settle and build a retreat of his own.
founder.journey1Desc: Venerable Thích Phổ Ứng entered monastic life as a disciple of the Great Master Huệ Nhựt, receiving the Dharma name Thích Nhuận Tắc and beginning years of study within the Mendicant (Khất Sĩ) tradition.
founder.journey2Desc: Like many monks of the Mendicant tradition, he spent years travelling and teaching wherever conditions allowed, deepening his practice before settling permanently in one place.
founder.journey3Desc: He founded Tịnh xá Linh Quang in District 4, Saigon, as a simple retreat for meditation and spiritual practice — the beginning of what would grow into a lasting place of practice and service.
founder.journey4Desc: He guided the temple through its 1963 rebuilding on a 1,250m² site, and by the time Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang assumed responsibility as abbot in 1983, had laid the spiritual foundation for the temple's later charitable work.

pastAbbot.intro: Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang (worldly name Trương Văn Phát) was born on April 15, 1943, in Bình Định Province. He entered monastic life in 1963 as a disciple of Hòa Thượng Thích Thiện Tấn, and went on to lead Tịnh xá Linh Quang as abbot for 37 years, expanding its charitable work before passing away in 2021.
pastAbbot.journey1Desc: Trương Văn Phát was born on April 15, 1943, in Bình Định Province, central Vietnam.
pastAbbot.journey2Title: Ordained As A Disciple Of Thích Thiện Tấn
pastAbbot.journey2Desc: At age 20 he entered monastic life, becoming a disciple of Hòa Thượng Thích Thiện Tấn and receiving the Dharma name Thích Từ Giang.
pastAbbot.journey3Desc: After two decades of practice, he assumed responsibility as abbot of Tịnh xá Linh Quang, continuing the legacy left by founding Venerable Thích Phổ Ứng.
pastAbbot.journey4Desc: He led the temple's major 1992 renovation, then founded a free clinic, an education center for children with disabilities, and in 1995 a free traditional medicine clinic serving the wider community.
pastAbbot.journey5Desc: Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang passed away on September 7, 2021, after 79 years of life and 58 years as a monastic, leaving behind a legacy of practice and social service that the temple continues today.

abbot.intro: Thượng Tọa Thích Minh Huệ spent many years practicing and serving at Tịnh xá Linh Quang before being entrusted with the role of abbot. In 2021, following the passing of Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang, he was formally appointed to continue the temple's spiritual and charitable legacy.
abbot.journey1Title: Practice And Service At Linh Quang
abbot.journey1Desc: Thượng Tọa Thích Minh Huệ spent many years in practice and service at Tịnh xá Linh Quang, becoming known to the local Sangha and lay community for his conduct and dedication.
abbot.journey2Desc: He took an active role in the temple's social welfare programs, working alongside Hòa Thượng Thích Từ Giang to support the free clinic and education center for children with disabilities.
abbot.journey3Desc: The Vietnam Buddhist Sangha formally presented the decision appointing Thượng Tọa Thích Minh Huệ as abbot of Tịnh xá Linh Quang, recognizing his conduct and contributions to the community.
abbot.journey4Desc: He continues to lead the temple's free traditional medicine clinic, its education center for children with disabilities, and its daily practice of meditation, sutra chanting, and dharma talks.
